question: Eight people sit in two concentric circles. Inner circle (facing in) has P, Q, R, S. Outer circle (facing out) has T, U, V, W. Each inner person sits behind an outer person. P sits behind T. V is 2nd to the left of T. R is 2nd to the right of P. W is adjacent to V. Q sits behind W. What is the position of S with respect to R?
explanation: 1. Outer(Out): T(0), V(2nd left = 2). 2. Inner(In): P(0), R(2nd right = 2). 3. W neighbor of V(2) = 1 or 3. 4. Q behind W. If W=1, Q=1. 5. S is at 3. 6. In a 4-seater, 0 and 2 are opposite, 1 and 3 are opposite. S(3) and R(2) are adjacent? No, check directions. S is opposite Q, R is opposite P.
trick: 'Behind' means facing the same way or occupying the same radial line. Here, radial line.
tip: Draw the circles as a 4-spoke wheel.

question: A certain number of people sit in a row facing North. M sits 5th to the left of N. O sits 4th to the right of N. P sits 3rd to the left of O. Q sits 2nd from the right end and 6th to the right of P. If there are 3 people between M and R, and R is at the left end, how many people are there?
explanation: 1. R is pos 1. 3 between R and M means M is pos 5. 2. M is 5th left of N, so N is pos 10. 3. O is 4th right of N = pos 14. 4. P is 3rd left of O = pos 11. 5. Q is 6th right of P = pos 17. 6. Q is 2nd from right, so Total = 17+1 = 18. Wait, re-calculate. M(5), N(10), O(14), P(11), Q(17). If Q is 2nd from right, N=18. If logic for 20, Q must be 19.
trick: The '2nd from right' is the most common anchor; ensure your N-to-O-to-P chain is solid.
tip: Position + (K-th from end) - 1 = Total.

question: Eight people A-H sit around a square. Some face in, some out. No two people at corners face the same direction. A (corner) faces in. B sits 3rd to the right of A. C is the only neighbor of B facing out. D sits 2nd to the left of C. E sits opposite D. F sits to the immediate right of E. How many face in?
explanation: 1. A(In, C1). 2. Corners alternate: C1(I), C2(O), C3(I), C4(O). 3. B is 3rd right of A(I) = Side 3. 4. C is neighbor of B (C2 or C3). Since C faces out, C is C2. 5. D 2nd left of C(O) = Side 4. 6. Final logic for directions results in 4 facing In.
trick: The 'no two corners face same' means C1-C3 are In, C2-C4 are Out. Instant direction fix.
tip: Use 'I' and 'O' labels for corners before placing people.

question: Six people sit in a hexagon. Each likes a different drink: Tea, Coffee, Juice, Milk, Soda, Water. Two seats are vacant. Juice sits opposite Tea. Coffee sits 2nd to the right of Juice. Soda sits to the immediate left of a vacant seat. Water sits opposite the vacant seat. If the vacant seats are not adjacent, who sits to the immediate right of Tea?
explanation: 1. 8 slots. V1 and V2 opposite (pos 1 and 5). 2. Juice(2), Tea(6). 3. Coffee 2nd right of Juice(2) = pos 4. 4. Soda left of V1 or V2. 5. Water opposite Vacant. 6. Result: Milk is at 7, right of Tea(6).
trick: Non-adjacent vacant seats in an 8-slot circle must be opposite to keep symmetry.
tip: Opposite in 8-seater = skip 3.

question: A family of 8 sits in two rows. Row 1: A-D, Row 2: E-H. A is the father of E. B is the wife of A. C is the sister of A. H is the son of G. A sits 2nd to the right of his sister. G sits opposite A. H sits to the immediate left of E. F is the daughter of A. Who sits opposite B?
explanation: 1. Tree: A(M)-B(F) -> E, F. C is A's sister. G(F) is E's wife? H is G's son. 2. Row 1: C _ A _. 3. Row 2: G faces A. 4. H left of E. 5. B and D at Row 1 pos 2, 4. 6. Final: B faces H.

tip: Draw the tree to know who 'A's sister' and 'A's son' are.

question: Eight people sit in a circle. Each likes a different movie genre: Horror, Sci-Fi, Comedy, Drama, Action, Thriller, Romance, Mystery. Action sits 3rd to the left of Sci-Fi. Two between Sci-Fi and Horror. Drama is 2nd to the right of Horror. Mystery sits opposite Comedy. Thriller is adjacent to Action. Romance is 3rd to the right of Mystery. If B likes Horror, what does the person opposite B like?

tip: If a genre lands on an occupied seat, reverse the 'between' direction.

question: Ten people sit in a row. Five face North, five face South. No more than two adjacent face the same. A is 2nd from left (North). B is 4th from right (South). C sits exactly between A and B. If C faces North, and all people between A and C face South, how many people in total face North?
explanation: 1. A(2,N). B(7,S). 2. C is at 4.5? No, 10 people. A(2), B(7). Middle is impossible. 3. Re-read: A(2), B(N-3). If N=10, B=7. Gap is 4. C is 4 or 5. 4. Following the 'no more than two' rule: N, S, S, N, N... 5. Total North will always be 5 in this balanced setup.
trick: The 'five face North, five face South' is a fixed total; the seating just arranges them.
tip: In 'balance' questions, don't over-calculate; the total is given.

question: A, B, C, D, E, F sit around a triangular table. A is at a corner. B is 2nd to the left of A. C sits opposite B. D sits to the immediate right of C. E is on the same side as F. If each side has 2 people, who sits to the immediate left of A?
explanation: 1. A(C1). B(2nd left) = S2-R. 2. C opposite B = S3-L. 3. D right of C = S3-R. 4. E, F on S1. 5. Left of A(C1) is S1-L. That is E or F.
trick: In a triangle, 2nd to the left from a corner lands on a specific side position.
tip: Corners are points; sides are segments (L,R).

question: Eight people sit in a circle. Each is from a different state: Bihar, Punjab, Kerala, Assam, Goa, UP, MP, WB. Kerala sits 3rd to the right of Bihar. Only one person between Kerala and Assam. UP sits opposite Assam. MP sits 2nd to the left of UP. Goa sits adjacent to Bihar. WB is 3rd to the left of Punjab. Who is from Punjab?
options: The one 2nd to the right of Bihar
answer: The one 2nd to the right of Bihar
explanation: 1. Bihar(0), Kerala(3). 2. Assam(1) or (5). 3. UP opposite Assam: If Assam=1, UP=5. 4. MP 2nd left of UP(5) = pos 3 (Kerala). Impossible. 5. So Assam=5, UP=1. MP 2nd left of UP(1) = pos 7. 6. Final: Punjab is at 2, 2nd right of Bihar.
trick: The '2nd to the left' from UP (pos 1) leads to pos 7, not 3.
tip: Clockwise is left for inside-facing circles.

question: Six people sit in a row. Three are seniors, three are juniors. No two seniors sit together. A is a junior and sits 2nd from the right. B is a senior and sits 3rd to the left of A. C is a junior and sits adjacent to B. Where is the 3rd junior?
explanation: 1. Pattern: J-S-J-S-J-S or S-J-S-J-S-J. 2. A(J) at pos 5. 3. B(S) 3rd left of A = pos 2. 4. Pattern must be S-J-S-J-S-J or J-S-J-S-J-S. If B(S) is at 2 and A(J) is at 5: pos 2 is S, pos 5 is J. This works in S-J-S-J-S-J. 5. Juniors are at 2, 4, 6. No, 1, 3, 5. Wait. 6. Juniors are 2, 4, 6. Pos 6 is the right end.
trick: The seniority pattern (S-J-S-J) is fixed once two people's roles and positions are known.
tip: Assign J/S labels to 1-6 immediately.

question: Eight people A-H sit around a circle. Some face in, some out. A sits 2nd to the right of B. C sits 3rd to the left of B. C faces the center. D sits 2nd to the right of C. question: A certain number of people sit in a row facing North. A is 5th to the right of B. C is 3rd to the left of A. D is 2nd to the right of C. If D is exactly in the middle and there are 15 people, what is B's position from the left?
explanation: 1. Total = 15. Middle D = 8. 2. D is 2nd right of C: C = 6. 3. C is 3rd left of A: A = 9. 4. A is 5th right of B: B = 4. Wait, 4+5=9. B is 4th. Check options.
trick: Middle of 15 is (15+1)/2 = 8. Use this as the absolute coordinate.
tip: N is odd? Middle is (N+1)/2.
